judged_text: The dedup filter compares raw guest strings with exact equality (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist in the same expression lowercases its entries — normalization is applied asymmetrically within one filter. Resubmitting an already-attendee email in different casing (John@X.com vs stored john@x.com) slips past the duplicate filter and creates a second Attendee row for the same person (duplicate emails, double calendar invite); the same asymmetry means the lowercased blacklist never matches a mixed-case guest string.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The dedup filter compares raw guest strings with exact equality (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist in the same expression lowercases its entries — normalization is applied asymmetrically within one filter. Resubmitting an already-attendee email in different casing (John@X.com vs stored john@x.com) slips past the duplicate filter and creates a second Attendee row for the same person (duplicate emails, double calendar invite); the same asymmetry means the lowercased blacklist never matches a mixed-case guest string.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but only the blacklist is lowercased (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`). Since `guest` is not normalized (and `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `.email()` without lowercasing), a mixed-case resubmission like `John@X.com` can bypass both the duplicate-attendee check (if stored as `john@x.com`) and the blacklist check, resulting in `createMany` inserting a second attendee row and triggering extra calendar/email updates.
